title: The Fantasy World Simulator — Design Reference Wiki

pages.title: A Run, Start to Finish
pages.blurb: The shape of a whole run — remembrance and your two domains, the opening spine and The First, the middle game, how either clock ends the run, and what the World-Soul carries into the next.

pages.title: Reaches, Spheres & Quintessence
pages.blurb: The two axes of every divine act — Eight Reaches (what you do) and Twelve Spheres (what fuels it), orthogonal by design — plus each Reach's virtue/vice moral axis, the Domain Capability word-ladder, and Quintessence as narrative centrality (not a ninth Reach).

pages.title: The Three-Beat Turn
pages.blurb: How a turn works — the world waits until you advance it; each turn runs scan → curated moment → aftermath in a load-bearing order; time in ticks (two hours, twelve per day); and encounters as rationed chapters, not per-tick rolls.

pages.title: Divine Actions & Prerequisites
pages.blurb: The five verbs every divine act reduces to (Create/Find/Change/Destroy/Control), why some action cards never appear (Reach outside your two domains — permanent; sphere misalignment; too little capability), the Generalized Action Targeting cascade, and the two reach signatures you acquire as story moments.

pages.title: Threads, the Court & The First
pages.blurb: The thread as a two-way bond — your investment depth (the five influence tiers) versus the mortal's awareness (unaware → intuition → faith → communion); the four court positions; The First's doom-clock-scheduled hero's journey; familiarity as player-side progressive disclosure; and why holding a thread deeply costs upkeep and makes you louder to rivals.

pages.title: Essence, Control & Sustained Power
pages.blurb: Divine fuel is per-Sphere and tight on purpose — where essence comes from (a baseline flow, worshippers, places of power, an Aspect's conduit) and how it splits along your alignment (0.35/0.25/0.40); Control as sustained commitment (upkeep, the slot cap, the three ways a working lapses); the usurp/destroy contestation trade where age is the defence; and the long strategic works that erode when neglected.

pages.title: Encounters & Aftermath
pages.blurb: The encounter as a framed chapter, not a die roll — the two shapes (branching and recurring) that share one UnifiedActionTemplate format; hex-granular awareness (see the hex, see everything on it); the single sigmoid→d100 resolution curve for peasants and gods, with doubles-based crits; aftermath as the mortal's trajectory shift; failure as plot; and the four encounter design rules. Player-voice layer over the deep encounters-agents-reference page.

pages.title: Doom, the Mandate & Omens
pages.blurb: The two clocks that pressure every run from opposite directions — the Doom Clock (seven archetypes, five Whispers→Culmination stages, escalations as world events) counting down to an Unmaking that always lands, and the Victory Mandate (three stages, your declared win-state) counting up; the one-pool-two-clocks tension made concrete by mandate checkpoints that bank counter-omens or owe doom severity; and omens as the pressure made visible.

pages.title: Encounters, Agents & Resolution
pages.blurb: Eight Reaches, Domain Capability, species, traits, attachments, the encounter types, the resolution pipeline, divine intervention, and the agent decision pipeline.

pages.title: Tick Cycle Reference
pages.blurb: All 12 orchestrator acts and 40+ phases in tick order, each with its reads, writes, and RNG tags.

pages.title: Action Catalog
pages.blurb: Browsable, code-true catalog of every ascendant-facing action template — spheres, reaches, costs, and real availability buckets.
